
```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| label: tbl-module-content
#| tbl-cap: "Content of the trial arms."

library(here)
library(gt)
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(gt)

Intervention <- c(
  "**Motivation**:\n\n- Exercises on identifying personal values and future aspirations in order to enhance treatment readiness and reduce resistance to change.\n\n- Psycho-education on improving decision-making by weighting long-term consequences over immediate rewards.\n\n- Based on structured goal-setting techniques, participants transform abstract desires into specific, measurable, and achievable objectives, increasing self-efficacy and clarity about their own needs and personal values in order to enhane treatment readiness.",
  
  "**Supervision and social relationships**:\n\n- Development of skills to build trust and collaborative working relationships with supervision officers, reducing resistance against community supervision and improving adherence to supervision mandates.\n\n- Identification of avoidance patterns that interfere with engagement in community supervision, using cognitive-behavioral strategies to enhance compliance with structured interventions.\n\n- Through guided exercises, participants examine the impact of adult relationships on emotional regulation and behavioral stability, targeting deficits in capacity for adult intimacy.",
  
  "**Emotion management**:\n\n- Identification of emotions as indicators of unmet personal needs, reducing impulsive reactions by linking affective states to underlying psychological demands.\n\n- Through mindfulness exercises and case examples, participants learn the importance of non-reactive awareness of emotions and connected bodily sensations, improving impulse control and reducing maladaptive coping.\n\n- Differentiation of emotional experiences and action urges using tools like the tension scale, fostering pause-and-reflect strategies to interrupt impulsive behaviors.\n\n- Creation of a personalized skill set, with adaptive, individualized responses to emotional distress, enhancing long-term emotional regulation and self-management.",
  
  "**Problem solving**:\n\n- Psycho-education on problem-solving deficits as a core component of self-regulation difficulties, understanding that challenges are manageable through structured, cognitive-behavioral approaches.\n\n- Guided exercises following the 7-Step Problem-Solving Plan to systematically identify, define, and address problems, enhancing decision-making and reducing impulsive or avoidant reactions.\n\n- Through video examples and case studies, participants practice distinguishing between changeable and unchangeable issues, generating realistic solutions, and evaluating outcomes.",
  
  "**Offense-supportive attitudes**:\n\n- Need-principle: Identification of three offense-supportive cognitions; the participant must choose three out of 16 pre-defined offense-supportive cognitions.\n\n- Psycho-education on how offense-supportive cognitions arise from selective attention to partial truths, reinforcing denial and minimizing consequences through psychological defense mechanisms.\n\n- Through cognitive restructuring, participants challenge distorted beliefs and promoting critical evaluation of harmful thought patterns in guided exercises.\n\n- Case studies and video examples illustrate real-world consequences of distorted thinking, bridging the gap between perceived justification and actual harm.",
  
  "**Sexuality**:\n\n- Psycho-education focus on the differentiation between healthy and problematic sexual interests and on how sexual preoccupation can increase reoffending risk.\n\n- The module addresses emotional congruence with children as a potential risk-factor, emphasizing the importance of maintaining emotional and physical boundaries between oneself and children to reduce relapse potential (relapse prevention).\n\n- Cognitive restructuring techniques are used to challenge distorted beliefs about sexual behavior, fostering insight and promoting adaptive, non-harmful thought patterns.\n\n- Through identification of high-risk triggers and personalized coping strategies, the self-regulation, self-efficacy, and control over problematic sexual urges and fantasies will be focused."
)

Placebo <- c(
  "**Physical activity**:\n\n- Psycho-educational content promotes the benefits of physical activity, identifies personal barriers, and set achievable goals to build motivation for physical activity.\n\n- The importance of motor skills, coordination, and balance, enhancing physical confidence and improving participation in daily and therapeutic activities is highlighted.\n\n- Through guided exercises, participants are introduced to break sedentary patterns, to increase awareness of health risks and motivated for a sustainable, active living.",
  
  "**Sports**:\n\n- Psycho-education provides the basics of muscle structure and function, increasing self-awareness of physical capabilities and enhancing motivation to engage in structured physical routines.\n\n- in guided exercises, intrinsic and extrinsic motivators are identified as well as barriers like low confidence or time constraints that affect adherence on personal training plans.\n\n- By reflecting on personal sport preferences in exercises, participants recognize how peer or cultural influences may shape physical activity choices, reducing susceptibility to negative social pressures.",
  
  "**Healthy sleep**:\n\n- Psycho-education promotes that sleep quality directly influences emotional regulation, cognitive function, and physical health, addressing impulsivity and emotional dysregulation that undermine sleep hygiene.\n\n- Understanding sleep cycles and physiological restoration helps link poor sleep to heightened stress, supporting those with external or sexualized coping patterns in developing healthier responses.\n\n- Practical, non-drug strategies are taught in exercises to manage shift work and jetlag, promoting consistent routines and environmental adjustments that support long-term sleep stability.",
  
  "**Dreaming**:\n\n- Psycho-educational content focus on the neuroscience of dreaming, including REM and non-REM sleep stages.\n\n- Through exercises like dream journaling, and symbolic interpretation, participants develop reflective practices that enhance awareness of dreams.\n\n- The module links stress, sleep disruption, and dream content, illustrating how chronic stress undermines executive function and exacerbates difficulties in structured thinking and solution generation.\n\n- Case studies highlight trauma-related dream patterns, showing how unresolved psychological distress and poor sleep hinder insight and cognitive restoration.",
  
  "**Nutrition**:\n\n- Adaptive: Psycho-education provides foundational knowledge on nutrition, digestion; the participant mus choose three out of six nutrition styles.\n\n- Through guided exercises, participants explore ethical, health, and environmental motivations for three out of 6 different nutrition types (e.g. plant-based diets, fostering empathy and prosocial decision-making).\n\n- Practical skills in meal planning and grocery shopping build confidence and sustainability, empowering lasting dietary changes that enhance psychological health and reduce behavioral risk.",
  
  "**Well-being**:\n\n- Psychological well-being is distinguished from happiness, focusing on meaning, inner balance, and personal growth, explored through reflections on identity, nature, music, and laughter.\n\n- Participants challenge the myth of universal well-being, recognizing its subjective nature and the importance of personal values, identity, and life context in shaping health and satisfaction.\n\n- Through exercises, participants explore the gut-brain axis, mindful eating, and hygiene practices, linking nutrition, self-care, and bodily awareness to mental clarity and psychological stability."
)

Module = c(
    "**Module 1**",
    "**Module 2**",
    "**Module 3**",
    "**Module 4**",
    "**Module 5**",
    "**Module 6**"
  )

# Erstelle die Tabelle
tbl_dat <- data.frame(Module, Intervention, Placebo)

# Erstelle die gt-Tabelle mit korrekter Formatierung
tbl <- gt(tbl_dat) %>%
  gt::cols_align(
    align = "left",
    columns = everything()
  ) %>%
  gt::fmt_markdown(
    columns = everything(),
    rows = everything()
  ) %>%
  gt::tab_options(
    table.font.size = 10,
    #quarto.use_bootstrap = FALSE,
    #quarto.disable_processing = TRUE,
    data_row.padding = px(1),
    summary_row.padding = gt::px(1),
    grand_summary_row.padding = gt::px(1),
    row_group.padding = gt::px(1)
  ) %>%
  tab_style(style = cell_text(align = "left"), locations = cells_source_notes()) %>%
  tab_style(style = cell_text(align = "left"), locations = cells_footnotes())

# save tbl as image
gt::gtsave(tbl, file = file.path(here::here("_tables/tbl-module-content.pdf")))
#gt::gtsave(tbl, file = file.path(here::here("_tables/tbl-module-content.docx")))
gt::gtsave(tbl, file = file.path(here::here("_tables/tbl-module-content.png")))

tbl

library(flextable)
library(officer)

ft <- flextable(tbl_dat) |>
  align(align = "left", part = "all") |>
  fontsize(size = 10, part = "all") |>
  padding(
    padding.top = 2,
    padding.bottom = 2,
    padding.left = 4,
    padding.right = 4,
    part = "all"
  ) |>
  autofit()

doc <- read_docx()
doc <- body_add_flextable(doc, ft)

print(
  doc,
  target = here::here("_tables/tbl-module-content.docx")
)
```
